data.narrative:
Clone Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Dhanush Radhakrishnan and Lucas Kozlik. The target operates within a sector comprising 9 private peers and 1 public comparable. The company has raised $7.1M to date.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable valuation anchor here. Using total capital raised as a proxy for current enterprise value ($7M), and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next financing stage, the analysis implies a valuation of $18M. Peer-median triangulation was not viable; while 11 same-sector comparables exist in Robotics & Manufacturing—including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI—the narrow filter for same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with similar valuation tiers yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 required). Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The single-method result supports a valuation range of $15M to $20M, with a median estimate of $18M. The lower bound reflects a more conservative 2.1x uplift from capital raised; the upper bound assumes a 2.9x multiple. Key uncertainties include the absence of a sufficiently dense peer cohort at identical stage and valuation scale, and the reliance on capital raised as an interim proxy for value in a Seed-stage company with limited operational track record. Validation through revenue multiples or margin-based methods is not possible with current data.
